sources.title: Climate Change Adaptation Planning for Castries, Saint Lucia
sources.organization: World Bank; ICF GHK, King's College London and Grupo Laera
sources.temporal_coverage: Castries hazard and adaptive-capacity assessment; many settlement and household indicators date from 2010-2012.
sources.methodology: City-level flood/landslide hazard, social and institutional vulnerability assessment with an adaptation investment plan.
sources.limitations: Baseline is primarily 2010-2012 and should not be treated as a current measurement of household conditions or institutional performance.

sources.title: Saint Lucia: Flood Event of December 24-25, 2013 - Joint Rapid Damage and Needs Assessment
sources.organization: Government of Saint Lucia and World Bank, with GFDRR and European Union support
sources.temporal_coverage: Assessment of the 24-25 December 2013 flood; report issued March 2014.
sources.methodology: Government-World Bank rapid damage and needs assessment spanning infrastructure, productive sectors, housing and social services.
sources.limitations: Rapid post-event assessment; some losses and interior housing impacts were explicitly considered incomplete, and the findings are historical.

sources.title: Disaster risk reduction in Saint Lucia: Situational analysis 2022
sources.organization: United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR)
sources.methodology: UNDRR risk-profile synthesis of hazards, vulnerabilities, capacities and systemic risk-governance gaps.
sources.limitations: Claims use the official report record's summary, not the linked 76-page report text; its findings are national rather than community-disaggregated.

sources.title: UN and Eastern Caribbean Partners Convene to Strengthen Prevention of Youth Crime and Violence
sources.organization: United Nations Barbados and Eastern Caribbean Multi-Country Office
sources.temporal_coverage: Regional consultation on a proposed youth crime and violence programme, 1 May 2026.
sources.methodology: Official UN report of a multi-country programme-design consultation and stakeholder remarks.
sources.limitations: Regional framing and programme design, not a Saint Lucia-specific prevalence study or evaluation of implemented activities.

claims.locator: PDF pp.73-74, named hillside settlements and vulnerability
claims.paraphrase: The Castries assessment identifies Black Mallet, Maynard Hill, Entrepot, Bocage and Pavee in Castries East, Bois Patat and Morne Dudon in Castries North, and La Pansee in Castries Central as poor, unplanned hillside settlements exposed to landslides.
claims.limitations: Settlement and household indicators largely use 2010-2012 data; they are not a 2026 risk census.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The report says poverty, poor construction and limited service access undermine crisis resilience; past disaster impacts were greater in poor areas.

claims.locator: PDF pp.86 and 93-94, institutional risk governance assessment
claims.paraphrase: The assessment describes Castries risk governance as reactive, with risk identification, reduction and adaptive governance weak and most investment focused on emergency response and short-term recovery.
claims.limitations: Historical assessment; it does not attribute this capacity gap to FCV or conflict.

claims.locator: PDF pp.6-7/66, event impacts and poverty distribution
claims.paraphrase: The December 2013 trough caused flash floods and landslides; Anse La Raye, Canaries, Soufriere, Micoud, Choiseul and Vieux Fort were heavily affected. The report says impacts were greater in high-poverty areas; over 550 people were displaced and about 19,984 directly affected.
claims.limitations: These are 2013 event estimates; the report notes that some housing damage was not captured.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The assessment explicitly says disaster effects were concentrated in areas with the highest poverty rates.

claims.locator: PDF pp.7 and 31-34/66, water and transport service disruption
claims.paraphrase: The storm damaged roads, bridges and drinking-water networks; sediment at John Compton Dam and pipe damage left the island without piped water for up to ten days in some communities. Larger Canaries and Anse La Raye systems were restored within a week.
claims.limitations: Historical response record; restoration timing does not measure longer-term service reliability or resilience.

claims.locator: Official report summary, findings on institutional framework, hazards and data
claims.paraphrase: UNDRR's 2022 summary says Saint Lucia's DRR framework includes NEMO, a multi-sectoral advisory council and a Hazard Mitigation Council; it also flags limited disaggregated data and lists civil unrest among the country's hazards.
claims.limitations: This is the official catalog summary rather than the full report; it identifies civil unrest as a hazard but gives no climate-conflict causal finding.

claims.locator: UN article, consultation rationale and regional youth-crime mediators
claims.paraphrase: A 2026 UN consultation included Saint Lucia among countries shaping a regional response to youth crime and violence. The article says regional youth risks are linked to structural inequality, socioeconomic exclusion, weak protective environments and unmet psychosocial needs, especially for boys and young men.
institutions: Saint Lucia Ministry of Home Affairs
claims.limitations: The evidence is subregional and records programme-design discussion, not Saint Lucia-specific rates or causes.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The UN says climate change, conflict and rising crime and violence collectively threaten regional social cohesion and citizen security; it does not assert a causal chain.

claims.locator: UN article, Joint Programme approach and next steps
claims.paraphrase: The proposed regional programme targets ages 10-29 with public-health and socio-ecological prevention, youth participation and gender-responsive interventions; in May 2026 stakeholders were still validating its design and governance arrangements.
claims.limitations: The programme was at design stage in May 2026; planned actions are not implemented outcomes.

search_audit.query: Saint Lucia subnational climate and disaster vulnerability in Castries hillside settlements, poverty and flood-affected communities primary reports
search_audit.outcome: The World Bank Castries assessment names landslide-exposed low-income settlements; the government-World Bank 2013 damage assessment reports district-level flood impacts and displacement.

search_audit.query: Saint Lucia climate, conflict, civil unrest, youth crime and social-cohesion mediators official sources
search_audit.outcome: UNDRR lists civil unrest in the national hazard landscape; a 2026 UN regional article links youth crime and violence to structural inequality, exclusion and weak protective environments and frames climate change, conflict and crime as collective social-cohesion threats without a causal chain.

search_audit.query: Saint Lucia civil unrest or violence effects on climate-risk governance, preparedness and adaptation delivery primary assessment
search_audit.outcome: Reviewed national and Castries DRR sources identify civil unrest, reactive risk governance and weak risk-reduction capacity, but none reviewed says insecurity or conflict obstructed climate adaptation delivery.

search_audit.query: Saint Lucia disaster response and climate resilience capacities, recovery and youth violence prevention official results or plans
search_audit.outcome: The 2013 joint assessment records water-system restoration and emergency response; the 2026 UN article documents a regional youth-prevention programme still at design stage. Neither establishes long-term outcome effectiveness.

gaps: The Castries household and settlement indicators are mainly 2010-2012; the 2013 disaster assessment is historical and incomplete for some housing impacts.
UNDRR summary lists civil unrest as a hazard, but reviewed sources do not establish a climate-related violence pathway or show insecurity obstructing climate adaptation in Saint Lucia.
The 2026 youth crime evidence is subregional and programme design remains in progress; it should not be read as Saint Lucia-specific prevalence or an implemented resilience result.
No current locality-level post-2023 flood or landslide vulnerability dataset was identified in the reviewed primary sources.
